title: ARIA roles must contain their required children
summary: An element has an ARIA role that needs particular child roles, such as list needing listitem, and they are missing. Add them or use native HTML.
problem: An element has a role that must contain certain child roles. For example, role="list" must contain role="listitem" elements. Without them, the parent does not form the structure its role promises.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users depend on this structure to hear things like how many items a list has and where they are in it. When children are missing, that information is wrong or absent.
steps: Find the parent element and its role in the scan result.
Check in the WAI-ARIA specification which child roles that role requires.
Give the direct children the required roles, or restructure so they are direct children.
Better still, use native HTML such as <ul> and <li>, which has the right structure built in.
whyItMatters: Broken structure gives assistive technology users wrong or missing information about content. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, and check the element in your browser's accessibility tree. The children should show the roles the parent needs.
